subject: Day 32: evening fussiness climbs; rotation plan
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 32. Evening fussiness is climbing toward the week-six peak. A working rotation between adults — who is on the witching hour, who is on the night feed — is the difference between an exhausting week and an unsustainable one.

Action items
- Agree explicitly on the evening rotation for the next two weeks. Write it down; do not negotiate at the moment of need.
- If Anoushka is breastfeeding, paced bottle feeding lets a second parent take an evening cycle without disrupting supply.
- Ask an outside adult — relative, friend, postpartum doula — to cover one evening or one night this week.
- Schedule the 2-month well visit if not yet booked. AAP Bright Futures periodicity: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Cluster fussiness in late afternoon and evening; smoother, more symmetric movements; social smiles.
- [low concern] Hiccups, wet sneezing, and a quiet startle to loud sounds.
- [monitor] Caregiver burnout — a short fuse, intrusive thoughts, dread of the evening — say it out loud before the worst night.
- [call within 24h] Sustained feeding refusal; forceful projectile vomiting; bloody-mucus stool.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Narrate one ordinary task end to end — making coffee, folding laundry — in full sentences during an awake-alert window. Romeo et al., Psych Science 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Lay him on a blanket on the grass in shade for a few minutes of tactile and outdoor-light input; stop before he fusses. AAP HealthyChildren on infant senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Read aloud on rotation; pause and look at him between lines so the reading has a serve-and-return rhythm. Reach Out and Read evidence base: https://reachoutandread.org/
- Tummy time 20-30 minutes a day across bouts. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 35-42: crying at peak intensity.
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit and first vaccines.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete

- Follows a moving object with eyes past midline
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Hold a small object 8-12 inches away and slowly move side to side. Eyes should cross the body midline.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-moving-object/complete

- Seems happy to see you when you walk up
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Recognition + positive affect. Often accompanied by limb-pumping excitement.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/seems-happy-to-see-you/complete

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete
